newsitem.title: ITALY: Nazi case to be re-tried in Italian military court.
newsitem.headline: Nazi case to be re-tried in Italian military court.

text.p: Italy's highest court decided on Monday that a military court should hear the war crimes re-trial of former Nazi SS captain Erich Priebke, a court official said.
Priebke, 83, is accused of complicity in multiple murder for his role in the SS massacre of 335 men and boys at the Ardeatine Caves near Rome on March 24, 1944. Seventy-five of the victims were Jews.

The Court of Cassation, Italy's highest court, had to rule on which branch of the judiciary was competent to hear the case after military and civilian judicial authorities both came to the conclusion that they did not have jurisdiction.
At his first trial which ended on August 1, a military court found Priebke guilty but ordered him freed, citing extenuating circumstances which triggered an expired statute of limitations.

He was rearrested that night after relatives of the massacre's victims laid seige to the courthouse. The verdict was quashed on appeal last October and Priebke is still being held in detention at a military prison in Rome.

No date was immediately set for the re-trial. Priebke will be tried with another former SS officer, 84-year-old ex-major Karl Hass, who was a prosecution witness at his first trial. He was later indicted on similar charges and is under house arrest in Rome.
